prompt.context: Your client is Air Co, a U.S. airline that has significant operations at one of the Chicago airports. Due to cold weather, the client's planes often have to be de-iced, but because the airline's de-icing need is very unpredictable, the client decided to outsource de-icing to Ice Co last year. However, Ice Co's performance has not been satisfactory.
prompt.question: The client is considering in-sourcing airplane de-icing, but currently does not have enough resources to perform the de-icing in-house. The client requires a 4-year payback on investments and wants to know if they should in-source or outsource the de-icing.

clarifying_info.q: What is causing Ice Co's performance problems?
clarifying_info.a: Ice Co takes too long to de-ice the planes, leading to flight delays. We cannot quantify the financial impact of this.

clarifying_info.q: How many de-icing events occur per year?
How long is the icy season?
How many workers would the client need to hire if in-sourcing?
clarifying_info.a: 150 people for the whole icy season (30 workers per month x 5 months). Workers must be paid for the whole month even if they only work one week. Each worker costs $4,000 per month.

clarifying_info.q: What is the total investment required to in-source?
clarifying_info.a: Refer to Exhibit 1 — it shows the breakdown of investment costs (Equipment, Supplies, Training). Total investment is approximately $3 million.

clarifying_info.q: What chemicals are used and at what cost?
clarifying_info.a: Ice Co uses 40 gallons of chemicals per event at $5/gallon. The client (in-sourced) would use 40 gallons per event at $4/gallon.

exhibits.title: De-Icing Cost Comparison and Investment Costs
exhibits.shows: A table comparing Ice Co and Client (in-sourced) across key cost metrics (number of events, fee per event, labor costs, cost per gallon of chemicals, gallons per event, cost per event), with some cells showing '?' for the candidate to calculate. Also includes a stacked bar chart showing the De-Icing Investment Costs broken into Equipment, Supplies, and Training components (x-axis in $M, up to 3.5M).

framework: Outsourcing costs: fixed contract fee, per-plane or time-based billing, procurement/governance costs
In-sourcing costs: de-icing equipment, de-icing chemicals, labor, airport fees, procurement/governance costs
Revenue/performance comparison: fewer customers to serve, better-trained staff, better-incentivized staff, faster de-icing times
Break-even / payback calculation: compare total in-sourced cost per event vs. outsourced cost per event, then divide investment by annual savings

questions.prompt: Calculate the in-sourced labor cost per de-icing event.
questions.guidance: Candidate should convert the seasonal headcount and pay structure into a per-event cost. Key steps: determine monthly events, determine monthly workers, compute monthly labor cost, then divide by monthly events.

math.setup: 150 workers hired for the full 5-month season. Workers paid $4,000/month each. 3,000 events/season over 5 months.
steps: Events per month = 3,000 events/season ÷ 5 months/season = 600 events/month
Workers per month = 150 workers/season ÷ 5 months/season = 30 workers/month

questions.prompt: Calculate the total cost per event for Ice Co (outsourced) and for the client (in-sourced), then determine the savings per event from in-sourcing.
questions.guidance: Candidate should add chemicals cost to the base fee or labor cost for each option, then subtract to find per-event savings.

math.setup: Ice Co: $300 fee/event + chemicals; Client: $200 labor/event + chemicals. Both use 40 gallons/event. Ice Co chemical cost = $5/gallon; Client chemical cost = $4/gallon.
steps: Ice Co (outsourced) cost per event = $300 + (40 gal × $5/gal) = $300 + $200 = $500/event

questions.prompt: Calculate the payback period for the in-sourcing investment and compare it to the client's 4-year requirement.
questions.guidance: Candidate should annualize the savings, then divide the investment by annual savings. Must explicitly compare to the 4-year hurdle.

math.setup: Savings = $140/event; 3,000 events/year; Total investment ≈ $3M (from Exhibit 1 chart).
math.answer: ~7 years — exceeds the client's 4-year payback requirement; in-sourcing does NOT meet the investment threshold as currently structured

brainstorming.prompt: The payback period of ~7 years does not meet the client's 4-year requirement. How could we decrease the payback period to make in-sourcing viable?

categories.name: Reduce investment costs
ideas: Lease de-icing equipment instead of purchasing it, lowering the upfront capital outlay

categories.name: Decrease labor costs (increase savings per event)
ideas: Restructure labor contracts so employees are paid for actual time worked rather than the full month
Explore more flexible staffing options instead of committing to monthly pay

categories.name: Reduce chemical costs (increase savings per event)
ideas: Negotiate a lower cost per gallon of chemicals from suppliers
Reduce the amount of chemicals used per de-icing event through process improvements

categories.name: Improve outsourced option instead of in-sourcing
ideas: Implement contract terms requiring Ice Co to meet pre-determined performance metrics
Tie Ice Co fees to meeting contract service level terms, creating financial incentive for compliance

recommendation: Based on the current numbers, Air Co should NOT in-source de-icing at this time — the payback period is approximately 7 years, which exceeds the client's required 4-year threshold
The client should instead renegotiate its contract with Ice Co to enforce performance standards and tie fees to service level compliance
risks: If Ice Co's performance continues to deteriorate, ongoing flight delays will impose unquantified revenue and reputational costs that could shift the calculus toward in-sourcing
Leasing or flexible labor arrangements may change the math favorably — further analysis required
next_steps: Explore equipment leasing options to determine revised investment cost and updated payback period
Re-negotiate Ice Co contract to include binding SLAs and penalty clauses for delays
Model alternative labor structures (flexible/part-time staffing) to assess whether in-sourcing savings can be increased sufficiently to meet the 4-year hurdle
